precepts.text: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools; all our lives we heard the songs of fools.
precepts.point: This "sing a new song" is repeated in Psalm 95, Psalm 96, and Psalm 98. All our lives we have been hearing the songs of fools, R&B, hip hop, and fake gospel. We never sang about the so-called black, Hispanic, and native Indian Israelites taking back over the earth; the Lord keeps reminding us to sing a new song unto Him.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
“It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.” All our lives we have been hearing the songs of fools: R&B, hip hop and fake gospel. We never sang about the so-called black, Hispanic and native Indian Israelites taking back over the earth.

That is why the Lord keeps reminding us, in Psalm 95, Psalm 96 and here in Psalm 98, to sing a new song unto him. He has done marvellous things, and his right hand and his holy arm have gotten him the victory; leave the song of fools and sing about that.

precepts.text: Christ destroys the nations without labor, light work by the law, and gathers another peaceable multitude, the Israelites coming back to their heritage as upright people.
precepts.point: He hath remembered His mercy and His truth toward the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God. The line, the gospel, is going out, so the nations understand that salvation is for the Israelites; we are coming back to our rightful position and our rightful name, and they are seeing it unfold in front of their eyes.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
His righteousness is openly shewed in the sight of the heathen, and all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God. Ezra shows how. “And Sion shall come, and shall be shewed to all men, being prepared and builded, like as thou sawest the hill graven without hands.”

“And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest; And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame: and he shall destroy them without labour by the law which is like unto me.” Christ destroys the nations without labour, light work, by the law.

“And whereas thou sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him”: that peaceable multitude is the Israelites, coming back to their heritage as upright people. The line, the gospel, is going out, so the nations understand that salvation is for the Israelites. We are coming back to our rightful position and our rightful name, and they are seeing it unfold in front of their eyes; that is how he has remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments; righteousness is keeping God's commandments.
precepts.point: He cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall He judge the world and the people with equity. Righteousness means us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them, and equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. By His righteousness He is going to give the people the justice due to them.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
With righteousness shall he judge the world. What is righteousness? “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Righteousness is us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them.

So when he comes to judge the earth, the standard he judges by is the commandments.

precepts.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness; the commandments are everlasting and are not done away with.
precepts.point: He cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall He judge the world and the people with equity. Righteousness means us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them, and equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. By His righteousness He is going to give the people the justice due to them.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The righteousness he judges with is everlasting, and his law is the truth; the commandments are everlasting and are not done away with.

That is why he can judge the world with righteousness when he comes: the law he judges by has never changed.

precepts.text: They that fear the Lord shall find judgment and kindle justice as a light.
precepts.point: He cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall He judge the world and the people with equity. Righteousness means us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them, and equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. By His righteousness He is going to give the people the justice due to them.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
He shall judge the people with equity. Equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. “They that fear the Lord shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.”

Those that fear the Lord find judgment and kindle justice as a light. By his righteousness he is going to give the people the justice due to them.

precepts.text: He that believes in the Lord takes heed to the commandment and shall fare never the worse; that is how you receive the equity, the justice, due to you.
precepts.point: He cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall He judge the world and the people with equity. Righteousness means us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them, and equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. By His righteousness He is going to give the people the justice due to them.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
“He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” Believing in the Lord is taking heed to the commandment, and he that trusts in him shall fare never the worse.

That is how you receive the equity, the justice due to you, when he comes to judge the people: by keeping his commandments, which is the righteousness he judges by.
